known.summary: `tarBytes` stages the manifest in the fixed folder `<tmpdir>/keys-manifest`, made with `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })`, not in a `mkdtempSync` folder (CWE-377). On a shared /tmp another user can make that folder first: then that user can read the manifest, which names each held-out key file with its SHA-256, or put a link at `MANIFEST.sha256`, so that `writeFileSync` writes over a file that the attacker chose. Two backups at the same time also share the folder. The pull request adds keys.mjs: the base has no such file and no key backup.
